response.sql: SELECT c.state AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS fraction_of_all_records FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY c.state

assumptions.assumption: A blank ('') state and a NULL state are different values, so they form separate groups, because grouping on c.state keeps them apart. The request does not say whether to merge them.

If college_id is duplicated in college, a player_college record matches each copy and is counted once per match. The duplicate rows would be in the same state or different states. This assumes college_id is unique.

The denominator is the count of all player_college rows, including rows with a NULL college_id or an unmatched college_id. The request states this directly. The numerator is cast to REAL so the division is not integer division.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat blank and NULL state as one combined 'missing' group, shown as an empty string.
alternatives.sql: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(c.state), ''), '') AS state, COUNT(*) AS matched_records, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_college) AS fraction_of_all_records FROM player_college pc JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(c.state), ''), '')
